Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
Prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) are rapidly expanding into weather and climate betting, now a $1.1bn market growing 500% YoY. Kalshi has partnered with the Weather Company to verify weather bet outcomes and embed market odds into the Weather Channel app. Scientists and ethicists raise concerns around gamification of climate disasters, perverse incentives, distortion of public forecasting trust, and moral hazard. Regulatory scrutiny is mounting, with a federal appeals court ruling states can regulate such platforms as gambling. The article questions whether crowd-sourced betting improves forecasting or merely trivializes climate suffering.

Q01. Is the content relevant to extreme summers/heat/dryness, specifically in a spring/summer/autumn context? How severe is the issue?
Relevance: IMPLICIT
Severity score: Spring 20, Summer 45, Fall 20, Winter 5

Heat is noted as the leading killer among US extreme weather events, giving it implicit seasonal weight.
